newsitem.title: FRANCE: Guerrillas again target post offices in Corsica.
newsitem.headline: Guerrillas again target post offices in Corsica.

text.p: Bombs blasted six post offices in Corsica early on Friday, hours after police said they had detained two suspects believed to have bombed seven other post offices on the French Mediterranean island a week earlier.
Bombs were defused in another three offices, police said.
There were no injuries and no one claimed responsibility for the attacks which bore the hallmarks of a two-decade-old guerrilla campaign by separatists.
The first five blasts, in the south of the island, were almost simultaneous and damaged offices in Sotta, Solenzara, Bonifacio, Pianotolli-Caldarello and Monacia d'Aullene.
An hour later a bomb exploded outside the post office of Ghisonaccia, in the east.
Bombs whose detonators had failed were found outside post offices in Travo, Aleria and Miglicciaro.
The Interior Ministry said on Thursday police from the island's capital Ajaccio, acting on instructions from anti-terrorism magistrates in Paris, detained two suspected bombers on Wednesday.

The statement, which did not name them, said they were supected of bombing the seven postal offices during the night of September 21, causing only slight damage. No one claimed responsibility for the attacks.

French Prime Minister Alain Juppe has decreed a crackdown on separatist violence. Guerrillas, blamed for bombings targeting public buildings and magistrates, have accused him of burying a peace process.
